questions.question: Which is a Command Staff position?
questions.rationale: Command Staff = Safety, PIO, Liaison. They report directly to the IC.

questions.question: The optimal span of control in ICS is approximately:
A 'Medical Group' is named so because it is defined by:
questions.rationale: Groups are functional; Divisions are geographic.

questions.question: The person in charge of an ICS Branch is titled:
A battalion chief arrives on scene. Command is transferred when:
options: C. The chief's rank is higher
D. A face-to-face briefing occurs and the transfer is announced
questions.rationale: Arrival alone does not transfer command. Brief, accept, announce.

questions.question: Unified Command is used when:
options: A. Multiple agencies share jurisdiction over an incident
questions.rationale: UC lets fire, police, EMS, and others share one set of objectives without surrendering authority.

questions.question: Which section would source extra oxygen cylinders and backboards for a prolonged incident?
questions.rationale: Logistics supports the incident with supplies, facilities, and equipment.

questions.question: An MCI supervisor is directly managing 11 ambulance crews. The ICS fix is to:
options: B. Ignore span of control in emergencies
C. Add a supervisory layer (e.g., group/division or unit leaders)
questions.rationale: When span is exceeded, expand the organization — modularity is the point of ICS.

questions.question: Who may immediately stop an unsafe act on scene without waiting for the IC?
questions.rationale: The Safety Officer has authority to halt unsafe acts immediately.

questions.question: An off-duty EMT drives to the scene and starts treating patients without checking in. This is:
options: A. Freelancing — an accountability and safety problem
questions.rationale: Everyone checks in and receives an assignment. Freelancers can't be tracked or protected.
